social.instagram_caption:
Wait… which tummy ache matters?! 😅

📉 In trials, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea were higher during dose escalation and decreased over time
🚨 Severe stomach pain that will not go away, with or without vomiting, and it may spread to your back → stop using tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider right away (possible inflammation of the pancreas)
🟡 Upper stomach pain, fever, yellow skin or eyes, or clay-colored stools → tell your healthcare provider right away (possible gallbladder problems)
✅ For anything that isn't one of those signs, don't stop or change your medicine on your own. If other stomach problems are severe or won't go away, tell your healthcare provider.

factcheck.summary:
The carousel's claims match the Zepbound Medication Guide and Prescribing Information:
- **Pancreatitis:** severe pain in the stomach area that will not go away, with or without vomiting, and may spread to the back. The action is to stop using tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider right away.
- **Gallbladder:** upper stomach pain, fever, yellow skin or eyes (jaundice) and clay-colored stools. The action is to tell your healthcare provider right away.
- **Severe stomach problems:** stomach problems that are severe or won't go away should be reported to your healthcare provider.

The don't-stop line and the ending disclaimer are copied exactly. Nothing gives dosing advice or tells people to stop on their own outside the label's emergency signs.

Both Lilly PDF links open, but the text couldn't be pulled from them. I confirmed the Medication Guide wording through search results that show the Lilly guide and the FDA label PDFs. The 6.1 line ("higher during dose escalation and decreased over time") I took from our own earlier checks. I did not re-read it in the PDF.

Two small wording fixes are listed below.

issues.claim: Tummy side effects change over time
issues.problem: Section 6.1 reports these as adverse reactions from the clinical trials. Calling them 'side effects' in the headline changes the label's wording. Our own rule is to keep the source's terms.
issues.fix: Nausea, vomiting and diarrhea changed over time in trials

issues.claim: Tirzepatide stomach pain: normal or call?
issues.problem: The hook asks whether stomach pain is 'normal', but the carousel never says how common stomach pain itself is. Slide 2 covers only nausea, vomiting and diarrhea. The answer the slides actually give is which signs mean you should call. So the 'normal' half of the promise is only partly delivered.
issues.fix: Change the slide 1 body to: "Common tummy effects vs the label's call-right-away signs". Change the title to: "Tirzepatide Stomach Pain: Which Signs Mean Call Right Away?"
